title: Any coefficient failure bound
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f$ be a sign-valued function on the Boolean cube, let $\\mathcal F$ be a finite family of subsets of $[n]$, and let the accuracy and confidence parameters be rational numbers in $(0,1/2]$. Draw uniformly an array of Boolean-cube samples indexed by $\\mathcal F$, with sample count determined by those parameters. The probability that at least one empirical Fourier coefficient indexed by $S\\in\\mathcal F$ differs from its true coefficient by at least the accuracy parameter is at most $|\\mathcal F|$ times the confidence parameter.
hypotheses_covered: target is a sign-valued Boolean-cube function
$\\mathcal F$ is a finite family of subsets of $[n]$
accuracy and confidence belong to $(0,1/2]\\cap\\mathbb Q$
